newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 15.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- The government has warned that Guy Ryder, International Confederation of Free Trade Unions representative, and three other overseas union leaders may be expelled soon if they do not stop actions supporting nationwide strikes. The Ministry of Justice has told them since their visas were issued for business purposes, their political activities are illegal, a top official in the prime minister's office said.

- Bus and taxi unions are scheduled to strike from 4 a.m. (1900 GMT) to 7 p.m.(1000 GMT) today, while subway workers in Seoul and Pusan have vowed indefinite walkouts until government repeals the new labour law. But unionists at subway lines 5, 7, and 8 in Seoul and express buses decided not to join the strikes.

- As labour strikes begin spreading to the public sector, the government, ruling party, and business community are coming up with iniatives to solve the crisis. Prime minister Lee Soo-sung and five ministers held a meeting to discuss legislation ammendments to a labour law, such as allowing multiple unions soon instead of in 2000.
